summary: This RFC proposes enhancements to the Exterior Gateway Protocol for a simple multiple-level routing system called autonomous confederations. It generalizes the core system to include several communities of autonomous systems and asks for comments.

eli5.summary: Groups of networks could be placed into bigger groups, like towns inside counties, to make route sharing more manageable.

questions: extending egp with multiple level routing
how can egp support multiple routing levels
what is the distance field in egp
how do confederations prevent routing loops
subtitle: Grouping autonomous systems into trusted communities for flexible routing.

tldr.problem: The Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP) enforces strict routing restrictions to prevent loops, but these restrictions are too inflexible for networks that want to share routes within trusted groups.
tldr.mechanism: Autonomous confederations group autonomous systems into communities that trust each other, allowing more flexible routing via a three-level distance metric (system-level, confederation-level, and global-level).
tldr.outcome: Networks can form confederations to exchange routing information more freely while still maintaining robustness against routing loops.

today: RFC 975 is an informational proposal for enhancing EGP routing. It was not widely adopted as an RFC standard, but the concept of multiple routing levels influenced later routing protocols like BGP, which uses the concept of Autonomous System Numbers within a larger Internet routing hierarchy.

sections.title: The Problem with Strict EGP Rules
sections.content:
The original Exterior Gateway Protocol was designed to be very simple and safe. It prevented routing loops by requiring that a non-core gateway could only pass along information about networks it directly reaches or networks that belong to the same system. This worked, but it meant that even trusted neighbors had to follow rigid restrictions. When networks needed more flexible routing—for example, when a system could only reach the core network through another non-core system—they were stuck.

This RFC proposes a way to relax these restrictions for networks that trust each other by creating autonomous confederations: groups of autonomous systems that maintain higher trust and can share routing information more freely.
sections.eli5: The old rule was very strict: you could only talk to the main office through an approved network. But sometimes you need to talk to neighbors in your group more openly.

sections.title: Autonomous Systems and Confederations
sections.content:
An autonomous system is a group of routers managed together using an interior routing protocol. They all trust each other and can share any routing information within the system.

An autonomous confederation is a group of autonomous systems that share a common security model—they trust each other at a higher level than they trust the broader Internet. Within a confederation, all networks can reach all other networks using paths that stay within the confederation. A confederation maintains better protection against routing loops than the original EGP model allows between arbitrary systems.

The key is that networks can be both directly reachable (a gateway directly connects to them) and confederation-reachable (reachable through trusted confederation partners). The distance field of EGP messages encodes this three-level structure: system-level routes get low values, confederation-level routes get medium values, and global routes get high values. This ensures that local routes are always preferred.
sections.eli5: A system is your immediate team. A confederation is a group of teams that trust each other. When sending messages, you always prefer talking to your own team first, then your confederation, then anyone else.

sections.title: Three-Level Routing Metrics
sections.content:
The RFC assigns ranges to the distance field in EGP Update messages. Values below a threshold (like 128) represent routes within an autonomous system. Values between that threshold and another (like 192) represent routes within an autonomous confederation. Values above that represent routes to networks outside the confederation.

This allows each confederation to run its own routing algorithm at each level independently. Different confederations can use different algorithms at the confederation level, but all must agree on the global-level algorithm. Within a confederation, networks are entitled to list all networks they can reach within the confederation in EGP messages to systems outside.
sections.eli5: Distance numbers encode where a route belongs: low numbers mean 'inside my system,' middle numbers mean 'inside my confederation,' and high numbers mean 'to the outside world.'

sections.title: Using the Distance Field
sections.content:
When a gateway processes EGP Update messages, it assigns a distance value based on whether the neighbor system is internal (same system), confederation (same confederation), or external. When a gateway sends messages, it inverts the routing database and partitions networks by gateway and system membership.

For each destination network, the router selects the gateway with minimum distance. Because of the distance-level assignments, routes within the local system are always preferred over confederation routes, which are always preferred over external routes. This natural hierarchy ensures that despite increased flexibility, routing stability is preserved.
sections.eli5: When deciding which path to take to reach a network, always pick the path with the lowest distance number. This automatically means you stay within your system if possible, then your confederation, then go outside.

sections.title: Backwards Compatibility
sections.content: The RFC proposes that the entire existing Internet, including the original core system, can be represented as a single autonomous confederation. This means the proposal does not require changes to existing implementations. Existing EGP implementations that do not interpret the distance field can treat all distances as equal to 192 (external), providing basic universe-level routing. Implementations that already interpret distance consistently can organize themselves into confederations using the proposed model.
sections.eli5: You can use these ideas without breaking old equipment: older systems just treat all routes the same way, while newer systems can take advantage of the confederation structure.
